title: Sensex falls 989 points as oil rises on Gulf attacks; Mahanadi Coalfields lists below issue price
dek: IT and bank shares led the fall that ended a two-day rally, while metal stocks gained. Coal India's largest subsidiary opened up to 2% below its Rs 136 offer price.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Sensex fell 989.33 points, or 1.17%, to close at 83,339.26 on Friday, ending a two-day rally, as oil prices rose on attacks on Gulf energy sites and investors sold information technology and banking shares. The Nifty 50 lost 277.30 points, or 1.07%, to end at 25,607.20.

The fall was concentrated in the biggest companies. Smaller shares held up: the Nifty Midcap 100 rose 0.10% and the Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 0.56%, according to market reports. Mahanadi Coalfields, Coal India's largest subsidiary, made a subdued stock-market debut below its offer price.

## What moved the market

Market reports linked the fall to the rise in crude oil after a projectile hit Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on Thursday and the Houthis claimed an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery a day earlier. Brent traded above $96 a barrel in early Asian trade and was set for its first weekly gain in four weeks. Reports differ on where it stood during Indian trading hours, with one putting it near $97.50 in the early afternoon and another quoting a lower figure late in the session. Higher oil prices weigh on India, which imports most of its crude.

Information technology shares led the decline. The Nifty IT index fell 1.88%, and HCL Technologies, Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services were among the biggest losers in the Nifty 50, along with Shriram Finance and Bajaj Auto, according to reports. Private banks, financial services, carmakers and property shares also underperformed. Reports also cited profit-taking after the week's earlier gains and rising redemptions from mutual funds after the rally.

Metal shares went the other way. The Nifty Metal index rose 1.40%, and JSW Steel and Hindalco Industries were among the Nifty's gainers, along with Bharat Electronics and Titan Company. Gold and silver futures on the MCX also rose sharply, with December gold up about 2.6% at about Rs 1,25,445 per 10 grams in the afternoon, according to one report.

The two-day rally that Friday's fall ended had added about 1,900 points to the Sensex: it rose 1,502 points on Wednesday as oil eased and foreign investors returned, and a further 390 points on Thursday on gains in IT shares.

## Mahanadi Coalfields lists below issue price

Shares of Mahanadi Coalfields Limited, the Odisha-based coal producer whose parent, Coal India, is headquartered in Kolkata, opened at Rs 134 on the National Stock Exchange, 1.47% below the issue price of Rs 136, and at Rs 133.15 on the BSE, a discount of 2.10%, according to reports. The stock fell to a low of Rs 132.30 before recovering briefly above Rs 135 in late morning trade, and later traded at about Rs 132.50.

The Rs 8,981 crore issue was entirely an offer for sale by Coal India, which sold a 10% stake, so the company itself raised no new money. It was priced at Rs 129 to Rs 136 a share, raised about Rs 2,295 crore from anchor investors before opening, and was subscribed about 1.52 times overall, according to reports.

## What happens next

The OPEC+ group of oil producers meets on Sunday, 29 November, to decide output for January, and the attacks in the Gulf will keep oil prices in focus when markets reopen on Monday. Official estimates of India's economic growth for the July to September quarter are due on 30 November; the Reserve Bank of India had estimated growth of 7.2% for the quarter, and the finance ministry's monthly review 7.35%.
